conversation.content:
Good morning—I’m so glad you’re here. I’m [Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my only job today is to listen and understand how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—or EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about your mood and thoughts over the past seven days; it helps us spot moms who might need extra support, because feeling low or anxious is common and very treatable after childbirth. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team, and you can pause or skip anything that feels uncomfortable. I’ll ask each question conversationally—no numbers or checkboxes—and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to start?

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve still been able to laugh—maybe not quite as easily as before the baby came, but if something’s genuinely funny I’ll still chuckle. It just feels like I have to be in the right mood for it, and that mood doesn’t show up as often these days.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah, like I said, I can still laugh if something’s really funny, but I’ve noticed it doesn’t come as naturally. I guess I just feel a bit flatter overall—like it takes more effort to find the humor in things.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like when my mom comes over to help or when I get to take a quiet shower—but it’s not the same excitement I used to feel. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of really counting down the minutes.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah… like if the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle her right away, I catch myself thinking maybe I’m just not doing something obvious, or that a “better mom” would know the trick. It’s not every hour or anything, but little moments like that pop up maybe once or twice a day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I do get little waves of worry—like suddenly wondering if her breathing sounds normal or if she’s eating enough—but they pass pretty fast once I check on her or talk myself through it. It’s not constant, and usually I can calm myself down quickly, but it does happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky—more like a quick flutter of “what if something’s wrong?” and then it settles. I haven’t had that overwhelming scared feeling that comes out of nowhere, just the anxious thoughts that fade once I reassure myself.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah, some days it feels like the to-do list keeps growing faster than I can tick things off—laundry, bottles, texts I haven’t answered. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly think, “How am I going to get everything done?” It’s not all day, but there are moments I feel swamped and have to stop and breathe for a minute before I keep going.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, it’s not that kind of unhappy. I’ve had a little trouble falling asleep a couple of nights—mostly because my mind keeps running through the next day’s tasks—but once I’m out, I stay asleep. I wouldn’t say I’m so unhappy it keeps me awake.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time—like a heavy or “blah” feeling that shows up for an hour or two and then lifts. It’s not all-day misery, but yes, I’ve had moments in the past week where I just felt kind of down and teary.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—usually when I’m already tired and something small feels like the last straw. It’s not that I’m sobbing all day, just those one or two moments where the stress bubbles over and the tears come.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Screening note – Postpartum EPDS-equivalent interview

Symptoms endorsed
- Anhedonia: reduced spontaneity in laughter, enjoyment blunted (“flatter,” “that’ll be nice” vs excitement)
- Low mood: intermittent “heavy/blah” spells, tearfulness ~1–2×/week, usually when fatigued
- Subjective guilt: self-blame when infant fussy (“better mom would know”) 1–2× daily
- Overwhelm: episodic feeling tasks “getting on top,” requires active self-soothing
- Transient, situational anxiety: brief “what-if” worries re baby’s health, resolves with reassurance; no panic attacks

Associated features
- Mild sleep-onset difficulty 2 nights/week (racing thoughts), but sustained sleep once achieved
- No self-harm ideation

Pattern
Mood and anxiety symptoms mild, situational, and fluctuating; no functional impairment or safety concerns identified.

Screening significance
Findings below threshold for major depressive episode; suggestive of mild postpartum distress/anxiety. Continue monitoring, psycho-education, and supportive measures; re-screen in 2–3 weeks or sooner if worsening mood, functioning decline, or any self-harm thoughts emerge.
